title: Television: James Paul McCartney | 1973
content:
Filming for the television special James Paul McCartney continued on 24 March 1973 at Elstree Studios.

The day’s tasks included a sequence for ‘Big Barn Bed’, which became the opening of the show. They were filmed miming before a bank of TV screens. The audio had been recorded at Elstree earlier in the month.

Also filmed on this day was the finale, in which Paul McCartney performed ‘Yesterday’ and an improvisation titled ‘Well, That’s The End Of Another Day’.

The day was also partly spent touching up the audio tracks recorded by Wings in February and early March. The band had recorded several songs, but the audio was not considered good enough to broadcast. A touch-up session was arranged, with Richard Perry producing.

Perry was producing Ringo Starr’s third solo album, Ringo, at the time. During this session he asked Paul McCartney if he would be willing to appear on ‘I’m The Greatest’. McCartney declined, due to the often tense relations between him and the song’s composer John Lennon, but he did show willingness to contribute a song.

McCartney had no spare compositions that would suit Starr’s vocal range, but said he would write something to order if he had a deadline. “So I said Wednesday,” Perry told the LA Times in 1974, “and he came up with his tune ‘Six O’Clock’.”

Quite coincidentally, Paul called and asked me to come to London to help supervise the musical tracks of his first TV special, because everything had to be re-recorded, and he wanted someone in the booth to help out the engineer, because TV engineers aren’t that experienced in rock recordings. And that was when we were going to London to continue work on Ringo’s album, so it all came together very conveniently.
Richard Perry
The Record Producers, John Tobler and Stuart Grundy

The backing track for ‘Six O’Clock’ was recorded at Apple Studios in London on 28 March 1973, with Paul and Linda McCartney among the performers accompanying Starr.
